features.summary: The plan grammar: its closed node set, how C# writes it and the TypeScript contract generated from it. Fifty-one kinds, each with one handler; every field required and none null as a state; a closed choice with no data a sealed class written as its text, never an enum; the typed contracts generated beside the grammar; the plan's version, 7, which the browser checks at boot, refusing a plan of another version or a script that is not JSON on its own; and the vendors map, shared by name across plans, since each handler carries its payload's place. Main writes version 3 and checks none, through a public converter, PlanNodeDiscriminator<T>, that only its own internal plan nodes name. The redesign makes that converter internal, writes version 6, parses any plan, and carries a payload kind on the vendor. Both lines generate plan.ts from the C# grammar.

meanings.meaning: D19.10's refusal, by the plan script. At boot, a plan script whose text does not parse as JSON, an empty one among them, or parses to no object holding a number version, such as [] or {}, is refused as a plan of another version is. Each refused script is one error: X19.3's message for a plan of another version, and for any other script an error naming the parse failure or the missing version. A refused plan's handlers never start. The page's other plans start, since each plan is its owner's and plans compose without merging (D14.2). Both lines throw out of the whole boot instead: main from its discovery (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/root.ts:64-70 at 623dd4a27) and the redesign from its own (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/plans/discover.ts:19-24 at 65fdf118d), so no plan of the page starts.

features.oracle: JSON as RFC 8259 defines it, which System.Text.Json writes and the browser's JSON.parse reads; TypeScript 6.0.3's exhaustive switch, a default of never, over the generated contract's unions; the DOM Standard's CustomEvent detail and UI Events' KeyboardEvent key for the payload's place; and check:kinds, which reads the grammar and plan.schema.json at 65fdf118d, schema.md's kinds table and Schema.tla's node set.

defects.defect: A refused plan script stops the page's other plans from starting, or two refused scripts show as one error, or one shows none (M14.D1).

promises.page: A net10 ward page whose layout renders a rounds fragment the app's distributed cache holds as an older release rendered it, its plan written at version 6: the fragment's Mark the round button, whose handler writes done into round-status. The test app seeds the cache with that fragment.
promises.outcome: round-status stays empty, and the console holds one error: "This plan was written for plan version 6; this page runs version 7."
promises.opposite: With the fragment's plan written at version 7, Mark the round writes done into round-status and the console holds no error.
promises.defect: The version 6 plan starts, as the redesign starts any plan that parses (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/plans/discover.ts:19-24 at 65fdf118d), so round-status reads done; or the error names no version.

promises.page: A net10 ward page whose own plan writes North into ward-name when Show the ward is clicked, beside two fragments the app's distributed cache holds: the rounds fragment of X19.3's page, its plan at version 6, and a vitals fragment whose plan script's text is cut off inside an object, the script element itself closed. The test app seeds the cache with both.
promises.outcome: ward-name reads North, and the console holds two errors: X19.3's message, and one naming the vitals plan's text as not JSON.
promises.opposite: With both fragments' plans whole and written at version 7, Show the ward writes North into ward-name and the console holds no error.
promises.defect: A refused script throws out of the boot, as main's discovery (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/root.ts:64-70 at 623dd4a27) and the redesign's (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/plans/discover.ts:19-24 at 65fdf118d) do, so ward-name stays empty; or the console holds one error for both scripts.

promises.page: The bench page renders a ConformanceElement at the id element, declared with ComponentVendor.Native, for room 4, and two partials, each with its own plan. The keypad partial's plan handles the element's Keydown, whose payload is the KeyboardEvent, the listener's first argument, and writes its Key into pressed-key. The signal partial's plan handles the element's Opened, whose payload is the CustomEvent its Open with room button dispatches, and writes its Detail's Room into opened-room.
promises.gesture: Click the element's key field and press 7, then click its Open with room button.
promises.opposite: Pressing 8 shows 8 in pressed-key, and the page rendered with the element for room 5 shows 5 in opened-room after Open with room.
promises.defect: The payload's place is the vendor's, one kind per vendor as the redesign carries it and merges plans' vendors by it (Alis.Reactive/Grammar/PlanDocument.cs:32-46 at 65fdf118d), or the first plan's for the vendor name both plans share. Read as the element, the native vendor's kind (Alis.Reactive/Vendors/ComponentVendor.cs:59-63 at 65fdf118d), each event hands its handler the element (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/objects/vendor-driver.ts:91 at 65fdf118d), which has neither a key nor a detail, so pressed-key and opened-room stay empty; read as a CustomEvent's detail for both, the keydown hands its handler the KeyboardEvent's detail, 0, which has no key, so pressed-key stays empty.

Main made it public, yet only its own seventeen internal node bases name it, in twelve files of Alis.Reactive/PlanModel (Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Reactions/ReactionGraph.cs:12-13 at 623dd4a27 among them), and the redesign made it internal (Alis.Reactive/Grammar/PlanNodeDiscriminator.cs:7 at 65fdf118d). Its capability, each node written as its concrete class with its kind, is `Html.RenderPlan`, which writes every node of the closed set with its kind (N14.2, D19.2).

verdicts.reason: The plan writer's inside, which no view, validator or component author writes or reads. Main made it public, yet only its own seventeen internal node bases name it, in twelve files of Alis.Reactive/PlanModel (Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Reactions/ReactionGraph.cs:12-13 at 623dd4a27 among them), and the redesign made it internal (Alis.Reactive/Grammar/PlanNodeDiscriminator.cs:7 at 65fdf118d). Its one behavior is a refusal, "Plan types are write-only.", and it carries no capability: C# never reads a plan, since the contract runs one way, from C# to the plan's JSON to the TypeScript that runs it. `Html.RenderPlan` is the plan's one writer (N14.2).
